latin_incipit: Omnis motor coelorum est anima sphaerae suae, faciens cum ea substantialem unitatem maiorem quam animae bovis cum corpore.
english_translation: Every mover of the heavens is the soul of its own sphere, making with it a greater substantial unity than that of the soul of an ox with its body.
charge: Averroes affirms that each celestial sphere is animated by its own soul, in intimate unity with the sphere itself.
defense: Pico accepts this as philosophical support for an ensouled universe and the reality of celestial intelligences.
exegesis: Echoing Neoplatonic cosmology, each celestial sphere has its own soul—more intimately united to the cosmos than animal souls to bodies. This affirms an ensouled universe, a key doctrine in Hermetic and Islamic Neoplatonism.

scholar_citations.work: Enneads V (on Intelligence and Intelligible Forms)
scholar_citations.quote: Every celestial body is ensouled by an intellect which contemplates the divine and imparts form and order to the cosmos.
Every sphere participates in an eternal intellective soul which is the source of its orderly motion.
The celestial souls are divine intelligences which transmit living forms and virtues to all terrestrial beings.

scholar_citations.work: The Arabic Influences on Early Modern Occult Philosophy
scholar_citations.quote: Islamic philosophers integrated celestial ensoulment into metaphysics of intentional influence, enabling magical theories of sympathetic transmission.

notes: Foundational to Pico's magical philosophy; establishes the celestial spheres as conscious, intelligent agents through which divine virtue flows.
